title: Best Google Ads Experts (2026): How to Hire for Search Ads
h1: Best Google Ads and SEM Experts
description: How to hire a Google Ads (SEM) expert: what the service should include, what to prepare, what drives the fee and the warning signs to avoid.
intro: Search ads can bring customers the same day they go live, and they can also spend your budget on clicks that never buy. The difference is usually tracking, keyword choice and who controls the account. This guide covers what to agree on before a specialist touches your ad spend.

faq.q: Is the ad budget included in the fee?
faq.a: No. The specialist's fee pays for their work. The money spent on clicks is paid directly by you to the ad platform, from your own ad account. Agree on a daily or monthly budget limit before launch.

faq.q: Who should own the ad account?
faq.a: You should. Create the account in your name with your payment method, then give the specialist access. If they build campaigns in their own account, you may lose the history and settings when the work ends.

faq.q: How soon will I see results?
faq.a: Ads can get clicks on the first day, but campaigns usually need a learning period and a few rounds of adjustment before costs settle. Ask the specialist what they will review in the first weeks and when.

faq.q: What is conversion tracking and do I need it?
faq.a: Conversion tracking records when a click leads to a sale, call or form. Without it, neither you nor the specialist can tell which keywords make money. Make sure setting it up is part of the job.

faq.q: Should I choose a one-time setup or ongoing management?
faq.a: A one-time setup suits small budgets if you are willing to check the account yourself. Ongoing management makes sense when you spend more and want someone adjusting bids, keywords and ads regularly.
